question: Why does sign letter height scale with legibility distance the way it does (1 inch per 10 feet rule)?
summary: Derived legible-distance ratios from Snellen acuity (5 arcmin floor) plus a reasoned real-world safety margin (2x-6x), predicting a 10-25 ft/inch range that lands almost exactly on the published USSC 10 ft/inch comfortable rule and the 25 ft/inch technical-max figure. Corpus states both numbers without deriving why they coexist; derivation explains them as the same acuity floor at two different margin settings.
